prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: High-fidelity desktop landscape product-design comp for a native macOS developer tool.
Primary request: Design the Operate mode of an AI-native iOS development environment as a blueprint-layer workbench. The agent-led task timeline is the dominant center workspace. A slim code/files rail sits on the left. A slim live iPhone evidence rail sits on the right. A horizontal verification strip spans below the main work area. The visual must feel unmistakably like a serious native macOS application, with a unified title bar and toolbar, dense but calm information hierarchy, excellent typography, crisp 1x pixel separators, and realistic desktop proportions.
Scene/backdrop: Straight-on full-window product screenshot, 16:10 landscape, no device frame around the Mac app, no surrounding desk or marketing scene.
Style/medium: Polished high-fidelity product UI mockup, native macOS SwiftUI/AppKit visual language, precise and implementation-ready. Blueprint-layer workbench means thin technical rules, subtle alignment marks, compact engineering notation, and a deep blueprint-blue working canvas integrated into a restrained graphite application chrome—not literal construction drawings.
Composition/framing: Full app window. macOS traffic-light controls at upper left. Unified toolbar across the top. Left code/files rail approximately 19% width; dominant center agent task timeline approximately 55%; right live iPhone evidence rail approximately 26%. Verification strip 90–110 px tall directly beneath all three panes. Toolbar should visibly contain repository/project selector, scheme selector, simulator selector, and the exact controls “Build”, “Run”, “Stop”. Current status must read exactly “Task running”. Use a segmented primary navigation with the exact labels “Code”, “Agent”, “App”, “Verify”, with Agent selected. Left rail shows a compact Xcode-like file tree and one narrow readable Swift source editor peek with line numbers. Center shows a chronological task timeline with a short user request, a compact plan, live tool steps such as editing, build queued, and simulator preparation; newest step has a subtle verified-green activity indicator but no completed claim. Right rail shows a live iPhone simulator preview with a Profile screen, a compact accessibility hierarchy beneath it, and one selected semantic element. Bottom verification strip groups four honest statuses: Build — Queued; Launch — Waiting; UI assertion — Waiting; Screenshot — Waiting. Include a generation label such as “Generation 3” and small evidence placeholders with em dashes, never fabricated passing results.
Color palette: Restrained graphite #17191D and #22262C application chrome, blueprint blue #174A78 and #236A9E for the working layer, cool off-white text, muted slate secondary text, verified green #3FA66A used sparingly only for active/healthy process indicators. No other accent colors except standard macOS traffic lights.
Materials/textures: Flat opaque surfaces, precise hairline dividers, very subtle blueprint grid lines only within the center working canvas, minimal shadow limited to native window depth.
Text (verbatim): “Code”, “Agent”, “App”, “Verify”, “Build”, “Run”, “Stop”, “Task running”, “Operate”, “Generation 3”, “Build”, “Queued”, “Launch”, “Waiting”, “UI assertion”, “Screenshot”, “Profile”.
Constraints: Prioritize legible real interface labels and believable information density. Preserve the exact four-area labels. Show a single cohesive workbench, not a collection of cards. Center timeline must be the unmistakable focal point. The iPhone evidence rail must look live but must not claim successful verification. Keep the screenshot professional, calm, technically credible, and visually balanced.
Avoid: gradients, glassmorphism, transparency, frosted blur, glow, neon, floating card grid, dashboard tiles, oversized rounded cards, excessive corner radius, marketing hero layout, fake success checkmarks, fake test counts, fake performance metrics, “all tests passed”, celebratory states, terminal-only aesthetic, generic web app styling, Windows/Linux chrome, 3D illustration, people, hands, watermark, logo, illegible gibberish text.
refinementPrompt:
Edit this existing high-fidelity native macOS UI comp with one targeted change only.

Primary change: Add a compact native macOS segmented primary navigation control in the unified top toolbar, immediately to the right of the “Operate” title and before the repository/project selector. The four segment labels must read exactly, from left to right: “Code”, “Agent”, “App”, “Verify”. Make “Agent” the clearly selected segment using a restrained blueprint-blue fill or underline. Preserve enough space by removing the existing back/forward arrow control if needed.

Preserve everything else exactly: full-window 16:10 landscape composition; slim code/files rail on the left; dominant blueprint-blue Agent Timeline center; slim live iPhone evidence and accessibility hierarchy on the right; verification strip below; all existing typography, graphite surfaces, hairline dividers, toolbar selectors, “Build”, “Run”, “Stop”, “Task running”, “Generation 3”, and honest queued/waiting evidence states. Do not alter the timeline, source tree, Swift editor, iPhone preview, hierarchy, or verification statuses.

Constraints: Keep all text crisp and legible. The result must remain a single cohesive native macOS workbench.
Avoid: gradients, glassmorphism, transparency, glow, floating cards, dashboard tiles, fake success checkmarks, fake metrics, illegible gibberish, marketing styling, changes outside the requested toolbar navigation.
